reader.requirement: A format 2 READ of an indexed file sets the file position indicator to the key of reference's value in the record area and makes available the first record with an equal key (for a duplicate alternate, the first of the set released to the file, by WRITE or by a REWRITE that created the duplicate); with no such record the invalid key condition exists and the READ fails.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.IndexedDuplicateKeyStatusSequentialOnly (ChangedIn 2002): at 85 a random READ of an alternate key whose next record duplicates it sets I-O status 02 (§1985:IX.1.3.4 GRL2.1); the key-of-reference assignment and record selection are not under the switch
the compiling program's edition baked on the connector, read by every DialectBehaviors.IsActive in the connector

reader.edition-search: read KeyedIoBinder.BindRead, KeyedIoEmitter.EmitRead and the IndexedConnector READ members; grep DialectBehaviors.IsActive|Edition|Year|DialectLevel over those files and the StatementValidation READ checks
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for selection and invalid key; the 85 random READ additionally sets 02 when the next record duplicates the key (GRL2.1)

reader.notes: FindRandom seeks the key's tree for the first entry with an equal key part; alternate entries order by (value, release ordinal) and Rewrite re-stamps a changed alternate with a fresh ordinal, so the first released record comes first. A miss returns 23 through the INVALID KEY branch.

refuter.evidence: Class c, 1985's own arm: IX.2.3.4 GR3 assumes the native collating sequence for an indexed file. q3pcs-001 (PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS EQ, with ALPHABET EQ IS "Z" "A" ALSO "B" "C"): native order AA, CC, ZZ, and READ by prime BB and by alternate BB both gave INV 23 (no equality through ALSO). --std 2023 printed the same (q3pcs-002). First-released order of a duplicate set: q6ord-002 covered DELETE then re-WRITE, a REWRITE from BB to CC and back, and a CLOSE and re-OPEN I-O; the set read back 09, 01, 05, 02, 10, which is the release order. q7ord-001 reopened that data file in a second program and appended 03; it came last, so the ordinals persist across runs. A REWRITE that keeps the alternate value keeps the record's place: q1keyref-002 Z1=02 05BBu5chg1 is still first of BB. cite.py: OK §1985:IX.4.5.4 GR17; OK §1985:IX.2.3.4 GR3; OK §1985:IX.4.5.4 GR14.
